title: Been vibe coding a dark fantasy roguelite in Godot, here's where it's at!
author: Afterlight_Games
selftext:
I've been developing Hollowfall solo in Godot and my Steam page just got approved and went live!

It's a dark fantasy first-person roguelite built around escalating arena waves and a 20 day Cycle. Each attempt costs a day and while some progression resets between Cycles, permanent upgrades carry over.

So far I've used AI pretty extensively throughout development. I use ChatGPT for, planning mechanics and working through design, Cursor for implementing and debugging code, and Tripo for generating some of the 3D assets.

I've gotten the core gameplay loop to a point where things are starting to come together, but there's still a ton I want to add. Right now I'm doing a pretty big polish pass, focusing on combat feel, animations, environments, UI, and getting everything to feel more cohesive.

This is my current early development trailer. Still plenty of rough edges, but it's pretty cool seeing Hollowfall reach Steam!

For anyone else building games with AI, how do you balance adding new features with going back and polishing what's already there?

[Steam Page](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5310380/Hollowfall/)

comments.author: TheUniverseOrNothing
comments.body:
I like this kinda stuff. I’d totally play it!

As for balancing features, I’m still working on that one. I’m always adding more features or polishing existing ones. And with new Opus 5.5 it’s done amazing work on my existing art so I just went redid all the art textures.
